To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the problem of finding succinct descriptions for multivariate sequences is hard, and (2) we can find good approximations of these descriptions very efficiently.
(1) it is feasible to discover concise, rich and accurate descriptions of complex multivariate event sequences; and (2) it is possible to do this in an efficient and scalable manner.

(i) we can succinctly describe multivariate sequential data in terms of a set of multivariate patterns that capture the (cor)relations in the data, (ii) this can be done in a principled manner that is based on the Minimum Description Length Principle, (iii) we can do this very efficiently, (iv) we can do it for both unlabelled and labelled data, and (v) the results we obtain are very good.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how can we succinctly summarise complex event sequences with rich multivariate patterns?
the discovery of succinct, high-quality summaries of complex sequential data, in terms of multivariate sequential patterns.
the following questions: How can we succinctly describe multivariate sequential data?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present an effective and efficient algorithm for discovering succinct summaries of complex event sequences in terms of multivariate patterns, which can be of great value in many domains.
we provide an algorithm that can succinctly describe complex event sequences with multivariate patterns, that is efficient and scalable, and can be used to summarise and visualise event sequences.
our approach is able to discover high-quality patterns that succinctly describe the data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a novel and efficient way of summarising complex event sequences, that is, sequences that have many interesting patterns and that are long, and that we do so in terms that are concise and that can be used to answer a variety of questions.
Ditto is the first method that can discover concise and rich multivariate sequential pattern sets from data, while being highly efficient and scalable.
Ditto discovers succinct, highly interpretable descriptions of complex multivariate sequential data, that are very efficient to obtain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to existing pattern discovery algorithms, Ditto can discover concise descriptions of data in terms of rich, multivariate, overlapping patterns.
, by using a rich pattern language, we are able to obtain concise descriptions that are much more meaningful and informative than those obtained with traditional pattern languages.

, in contrast to previous approaches to summarising multivariate sequential data, we can provide succinct descriptions of data in terms of rich patterns that can capture complex relations between sequences.
